creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Fencil decision chrome-colors (owner-nodded, 2026-11-08): Muster has no theme of its own, and the redesign's new surfaces take their colors from settings that already exist.

- The agent list keeps macOS's own colors, as it does today.
- The pane area, pane headers and the conversation view included, takes the terminal's background and foreground from [colors]. A header is the background shifted a little toward the foreground, so it reads as part of the pane. The owner's config sets neither, so his headers would come from the renderer's default background.
- A tint for a state, behind a blocked row or header, is that state's agent_* color mixed into the surface it sits on, so changing agent_blocked recolors the tint too.

No color setting is added. One pure function derives every color, with a minimum contrast between text and the surface under it, and is tested against a light theme, a dark theme and the renderer's default: a computed color can lose contrast on an unusual theme, such as a light terminal beside a dark-mode sidebar. The rows, pane-header, conversation and banner cards all draw with it.

## Plan (reviewed 2026-11-08)

From the plan for the redesign, step 5; the parent card a_2wKW8eBfM has its overall shape, order and checks.

`[colors] background` and `foreground` reach the shell (`Core.read` into
`MusterRenderer.Appearance`) but nothing keeps them for chrome code, and when the file sets neither,
nothing reads the renderer's default.

- `PaneAppearance` keeps the pane half of the appearance it adopts, beside `Core.Chrome`.
- For a color the file leaves out, `Renderer` reads the effective value from libghostty with
  `ghostty_config_get(config, &color, "background", ...)`, which Muster has not called before; the
  call is wrapped in `Renderer` so nothing else touches libghostty's config.
- One pure function, `ChromePalette.make(terminal:agents:appearance:)`, returns every derived color:
  header background (terminal background moved toward the foreground), header text and its dimmer
  step, the tint for each state on each surface it sits on (the agent list's background and a
  header's), and the keycap fill and edge. Text colors are pushed toward the foreground until they
  reach 4.5:1 against their surface.
- Swift tests run it against a dark theme, a light theme and the renderer's default, and assert the
  contrast floor for every text and surface pair.
title: Derive the redesign's colors from the terminal colors, macOS and the state legend
